# m.stocks.last_quote

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

The latest national best bid and offer of each US-listed stock.

Call it from a session `m`:

```python
m.stocks.last_quote(symbols)
```

- Query methods: `fetch()`, `poll()`
- Read from: REST
- `poll()` by default: `dm.PollMode.REPLACE`, which holds only the latest poll's rows, one row per `Symbol`
- `poll(mode=dm.PollMode.APPEND)`: appends each new state of a row, identified by `Symbol` and `Timestamp`

[Dataset index](README.md)

## Arguments

A linked argument follows the [shared rules](README.md#shared-arguments) on the dataset index.

| Argument | Description |
| --- | --- |
| [`symbols`](README.md#symbols) | Stock tickers; `dm.ALL` is refused (use `m.stocks.snapshots(dm.ALL)`). |

## Plans

How recent the data is on each of Massive's plans, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Last Quote (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| Stocks Basic | Not included |
| Stocks Starter | Not included |
| Stocks Developer | Not included |
| Stocks Advanced | Real-time |
| Stocks Business | Not included |
| Stocks Business + Expansion | Real-time |

## Columns

| Column | Type | Description |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `Symbol` | String | The instrument, in the library's canonical symbol form. From REST `T`: "The exchange symbol that this item is traded under." |
| `Date` | String | The trading day of the row, as ISO yyyy-MM-dd text: the New York date of `Timestamp`. |
| `Timestamp` | Instant | The row's primary time, as an Instant. From REST `t`: "The nanosecond accuracy SIP Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the SIP received this message from the exchange which produced it." |
| `RawSymbol` | String | The symbol exactly as Massive sent it, on a row whose spelling the library cannot read as the dataset's class (its `Symbol` is then null); null on every other row. Present unless the session's `unreadable_symbols` is `dm.OnError.RAISE`, which fails on such a row instead. |
| `BidPrice` | double | The bid price. |
| `BidSize` | double | The bid size. This represents the number of shares buyers are bidding for at the given bid price. |
| `AskPrice` | double | The ask price. |
| `AskSize` | double | The ask size. This represents the number of shares sellers are offering at the given ask price. |
| `BidExchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. |
| `AskExchange` | long | The exchange ID. See Exchanges (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/exchanges) for Massive's mapping of exchange IDs. |
| `Conditions` | long[] | A list of condition codes. See Stocks Condition Codes (https://massive.com/docs/rest/stocks/market-operations/condition-codes) for what each code means. |
| `Indicators` | long[] | A list of indicator codes. See the Conditions and Indicators (https://massive.com/glossary/conditions-indicators) glossary for what each code means. |
| `ParticipantTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy Participant/Exchange Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the quote was actually generated at the exchange. |
| `SequenceNumber` | long | The sequence number represents the sequence in which message events happened. These are increasing and unique per ticker symbol, but will not always be sequential (e.g., 1, 2, 6, 9, 10, 11). |
| `Tape` | long | There are 3 tapes which define which exchange the ticker is listed on. These are integers in our objects which represent the letter of the alphabet. Eg: 1 = A, 2 = B, 3 = C. * Tape A is NYSE listed securities * Tape B is NYSE ARCA / NYSE American * Tape C is NASDAQ |
| `TrfTimestamp` | Instant | The nanosecond accuracy TRF(Trade Reporting Facility) Unix Timestamp. This is the timestamp of when the trade reporting facility received this message. |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. |
